sections.h2: Who runs the Edgecombe County Register of Deeds and how do I reach it?
sections.html:
The Edgecombe County Register of Deeds is the county office that records and maintains births, deaths, marriages, military discharges, notaries, maps and real estate transactions. The county page gives the phone as (252) 641-7924, so call before you travel to confirm counter hours and the street address.

The office describes itself as governed by three state bodies: the Legislature, the Secretary of State and North Carolina Vital Records. It serves attorneys, land surveyors, realtors, funeral homes, genealogists and the public. Tarboro is the county seat, and the county describes itself as a rural county about an hour east of Raleigh with a farming base and some advanced manufacturing.

Selling a house in Edgecombe County means the deed ends up in this office, usually sent by a closing attorney. North Carolina voters elect each county's register of deeds every two years under G.S. 161-1. Knowing the fee list and the local rules in the next sections keeps that step quick.

sections.h2: What does the Edgecombe County Register of Deeds charge?
sections.html:
The standard recording fee is $26.00 for the first 15 pages with $4.00 for each extra page, and the county prints the excise tax line as $1.00 per $500.00. Everything below comes from the office's own fee schedule PDF.

Edgecombe County Register of Deeds fee schedule as printed (source: edgecombecountync.gov fee schedule PDF)
ServiceFee as printed
Instruments in general, except deeds of trust and mortgages$26.00 for 1st 15 pages, $4.00 each page after 15
Deeds of trust and mortgages$64.00 for 1st 35 pages, $4.00 each page after 35
Excise tax$1.00 per $500.00
Nonstandard document$25.00 + recording fee
Plats$21.00
Certified copies$5.00 first page, $2.00 each additional
Uncertified copies$.10 per page
Map copies$.50 for 11 x 17, $1.00 for 18 x 24
SatisfactionNo fee

The office adds that filings and requests are processed the same day received, and it asks mail customers to enclose a self addressed stamped envelope.

sections.h2: Does Edgecombe County require tax certification before a deed is recorded?
sections.html:
Yes, with one exception. The fee schedule says that under an Edgecombe County resolution, every deed must carry a tax certification from the Tax Collector's office before it is recorded unless a specific attorney statement appears on the instrument.

The exception is a line stating the deed was prepared by a licensed North Carolina attorney and that any delinquent taxes will be paid to the county tax collector by the closing attorney when closing proceeds are disbursed. An attorney preparing your deed can supply that statement. A seller who prepares a deed without an attorney should visit the Tax Collector first and get the certification the resolution calls for.

  • With an attorney: the preparer statement on the deed covers the requirement, and the attorney settles any back taxes from your proceeds.
  • Without an attorney: obtain the tax certification from the Edgecombe County Tax Collector before you bring the deed in.

sections.h2: Can I record a deed electronically in Edgecombe County?
sections.html:
Yes. The county's E-Recording page says the office accepts electronic recording through its vendor Simplifile, and it also points to CSC eRecording Solutions. Title companies and law firms that already have an account can send the deed and have it recorded without a courier.

A seller without an account should ask the closing attorney to submit it. Paper deeds still follow the state filing standards the county posts as a PDF on its Real Estate page, along with an Assumed Name form and property check instructions.

sections.h2: What personal information must stay off a document I file?
sections.html:
Do not put Social Security, employer taxpayer identification, driver's license, state identification, passport, bank account, credit card or debit card numbers, PINs or passwords in a document filed for recording. The county's notice cites G.S. 132-1.10(g)(1) and allows such a number only when the law or a court order requires it, or when it is redacted to its last four digits.

Whatever is filed becomes part of the county's official records, so read the document before signing it and ask the preparer to remove anything that should not be there.

sections.h2: What happens to farm or timber land in the use value program when the deed records?
sections.html:
The deed date starts a clock. Edgecombe County's Present Use Value page says a buyer who wants to keep land in the program must file an application within 60 days of the transfer, and it treats the date the deed is recorded at the Edgecombe County Register of Deeds as the transfer date.

The same page explains that deferred taxes for the year of the change and the three prior years become due with interest if the land leaves the program, and that the new owner must accept the liability for deferred taxes, even for years before the sale. If you own such land, ask the Tax Assessor for the status before you list or accept an offer.

  • Agricultural land needs at least 10 cultivated acres, and forest land needs at least 20 forested acres with a management plan.
  • Agricultural income must average at least $1000 per year over the past three years.
  • A sale to a non-qualifying owner can take the land out of the program.

sections.h2: What does a certified copy cost and how do I order vital records?
sections.html:
Certified copies of birth, death and marriage certificates cost $10 each. The office offers online ordering through Permitium/AIS, which adds a $3.35 convenience fee per order plus card fees, and mail orders are still accepted using the county's application form.

The office holds birth and death records starting in October 1913 and marriage records starting in 1867, per its Vital Records page.

sections.h2: How do Edgecombe County property taxes tie into a deed?
sections.html:
The Edgecombe County Tax Collector's office collects tax on real estate, personal property and motor vehicles for the county, 14 fire districts, one drainage district and eight towns. Its responsibilities include preparing statements of taxes due for attorneys and other real estate professionals, which a closing attorney can request before a sale closes.

The office also issues mobile home moving permits and handles delinquent accounts, including foreclosure. Questions about taxes paid or owed go to the Tax Collector at (252) 641-7810, while questions about a bill's value go to the Tax Assessor at (252) 641-7855. Our Edgecombe County property tax guide covers the rates, listing rules and appeal steps in detail.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about Edgecombe County?
sections.html:
Edgecombe County is small and rural, and the Census Bureau's QuickFacts table lists these figures for it.

  • Population: 49,121 in the July 2025 estimate, with 23,604 housing units and 505.44 square miles of land.
  • Owner-occupied housing rate of 60.8% and a median owner-occupied value of $125,100 for 2020 to 2024.
  • Median household income of $51,265 and median gross rent of $858.
  • Residents aged 65 and over make up 23.1% of the population.
  • Building permits in 2025: 53.

Because recording fees are set by statute, a house worth $125,100 pays the same page charge as one worth many times more. The excise tax is the line that grows with the price.

faqs.q: Does Edgecombe County charge to record a satisfaction of a deed of trust?
faqs.a: No. The county fee schedule lists satisfaction as no fee, so a mortgage payoff at closing adds no recording charge for the release.

faqs.q: How much is the excise tax in Edgecombe County?
faqs.a: The county prints the excise tax as $1.00 per $500.00. State law puts that tax on the seller, who pays the register of deeds before the deed is recorded, and the office collects it with the deed.

faqs.q: Can I record a deed in Edgecombe County without a tax certification?
faqs.a: Only if the deed carries the attorney preparer statement. The county's resolution requires a tax certification from the Tax Collector's office unless the instrument states that a licensed North Carolina attorney prepared it and that the closing attorney will pay any delinquent taxes from closing proceeds.

faqs.q: How do I order a certified copy of a vital record from the Edgecombe County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Order online through the office's Permitium/AIS system or by mailing the application for certified copy. Each copy is $10, and the online route adds a $3.35 convenience fee plus card fees.

faqs.q: Does the Edgecombe County Register of Deeds accept e-recording?
faqs.a: Yes. The office accepts e-recording through Simplifile and lists CSC eRecording Solutions as another route. Ask your closing attorney or title company to submit the deed through their account.
